newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were steady to higher in moderate trade with most traders sidelined due mainly to an absence of fresh incentives, dealers said on Monday.
Most traders were waiting for Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for fresh clues to monetary policy, they said.

"Rates were steady to a little bit higher in the morning on some position adjustments. Basically, everyone is waiting for some more clues to market direction from the outcome of Tuesday's FOMC meeting," a local dealer said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday was unchanged from last Friday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
Tuesday/Wednesday and week-fixed rose 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from last Friday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16, nine-months unchanged at 6-1/8 6 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/4 6-1/8 percent.
